stak-energy-north-slope-ak.name: Stak Energy North Slope Data Center
stak-energy-north-slope-ak.powered_by: On-site natural gas generation (off-grid, new pipeline from North Slope reserves)
stak-energy-north-slope-ak.water_notes: Arctic air cooling reduces water consumption by 90%+ compared to industry norms per company. Sub-freezing average temperatures enable free air cooling.
stak-energy-north-slope-ak.source: Alaska's North Slope Proposed as Home for Massive AI Data Center
stak-energy-north-slope-ak.notes: Preliminary state land lease approval covers 715.4 acres (corrected from 640; one square mile = 640 acres exactly but the approved lease footprint is 715.4 acres per Alaska Beacon). Campus is approximately 26 miles south of Deadhorse/Prudhoe Bay off the Dalton Highway (corrected from 25 miles). Supports AI training, cloud computing, and HPC. 3 GW is the project's claimed ultimate potential; $500M is Phase 1 capital. Coordinates estimated (~26 miles south of Prudhoe Bay 70.2N/148.5W); exact site not publicly disclosed.

google-jackson-county-stevenson-al.name: Google Jackson County Campus
google-jackson-county-stevenson-al.water_notes: Site sits on Guntersville Reservoir (Tennessee River), which historically cooled the coal plant; data-center cooling type not publicly confirmed.
google-jackson-county-stevenson-al.source: Google Blog: Alabama Investment - Jackson County Campus Expansion (June 2026)
google-jackson-county-stevenson-al.notes: Campus operational since 2019 at the former TVA Widows Creek coal-plant site (~4.8 mi east of Stevenson). Recorded status is 'operational' (the campus is built and running); a $1.5B expansion announced June 15 2026 is under construction for 2026-2027 (captured in statusHistory). CAPACITY OMITTED: the widely cited 300 MW is Google's contracted new generation across the Tennessee Valley REGION, not a campus-specific figure. TVA partnership also includes a 2025 Kairos Power agreement for up to 50 MW of advanced nuclear for Google's AL/TN data centers (~2035). Construction workforce of 1,000+ is a projection (in notes, not jobs). Baxtel labels this 'Google Bridgeport'; TVA/Wikipedia/postal (35772) place Widows Creek near Stevenson - Stevenson used. 360-acre site; coordinates from the Widows Creek plant.

nebius-bhm01-birmingham-al.name: Nebius Birmingham AI Factory (BHM01)
nebius-bhm01-birmingham-al.source: Nebius x Birmingham, Alabama - Official Project Page
nebius-bhm01-birmingham-al.notes: Nebius Group's Birmingham AI Factory (site code BHM01); distinct from nebius-vineland-nj and nebius-independence-mo. Capacity phased: Phase I = 100 MW (targeted H2 2026), Phase II adds 200 MW (full 300 MW by 2027-2028). Land acquisition $90M confirmed (2025-09-30); ~$855M in construction permits issued (April 2026) with $2.1B more under review; total capex described as 'tens of billions' (a projection) - so investmentUsd is omitted. ~100-125 projected permanent jobs (in notes, not jobs). Site: former Regions Lakeshore Operations Center (~80 acres) acquired from UAB, Regions Bank, and U.S. Steel; general contractor Hoar Construction. Coordinates address-approximate (201 Milan Pkwy, Oxmoor Corporate Park).

google-west-memphis-ar.name: Google West Memphis Data Center Campus
google-west-memphis-ar.water_notes: Graywater plant planned to reuse water for equipment cooling

google-west-memphis-ar.notes: Campus on Bolliger Road, West Memphis. Coordinates approximate for the Bolliger Road industrial area. $4B is Phase 1 through 2027; total planned investment is $10B, which would be the largest private capital investment in Arkansas history. Five data center buildings on 920-acre campus footprint within a 1,178-acre site (per U.S. Army Corps of Engineers filing). Fixes: (1) removed unsourced 5,000 construction jobs figure — AEDC states only 'thousands'; (2) corrected energy.source from 'solar' to 'grid' — facility draws from Entergy Arkansas; Arkansas Cypress Solar is a companion renewable project; (3) corrected landAcres from 1,200 to 1,178 per Army Corps filing.

google-port-of-little-rock-data-center-a.name: Port of Little Rock Data Center

aws-laveen-az.name: AWS Laveen Data Center Campus

aligned-phx13-glendale-az.name: Aligned PHX-13
aligned-phx13-glendale-az.water_notes: Aligned Delta-cube closed-loop air-cooling arrays with water recycling (no evaporative draw); DeltaFlow liquid cooling planned for dense AI workloads. A marketed '>73% water reduction' is versus the site's prior agricultural (rose-farm) use, not a data-center withdrawal figure -> no MGD recorded.
aligned-phx13-glendale-az.source: Aligned Data Centers breaks ground on Glendale, expanding Arizona infrastructure
aligned-phx13-glendale-az.notes: PHX-13, a 72 MW campus in Glendale, Maricopa County. Coordinates are the Glendale area centroid. Land acquired for $86.5M (100 acres at 8785 N Reems Rd, Dec 2024, from LXP Industrial Trust) - land cost, not campus capex -> investmentUsd omitted. No job counts disclosed -> jobs honest-zero. The campus likely uses Arizona's statutory data-center TPT exemption (A.R.S. 41-1519), but no ACA certification or GPLET agreement for this campus is public -> subsidy honest-zero.

flexential-denver-centennial-den05-co.notes: Address 12500 E Arapahoe Rd, Centennial CO 80112. Confirmed via DataCenterJournal (DEN05) and datacenterHawk.

nextnrg-nassau-county-data-center-energy.name: NextNRG Nassau County Data Center & Energy Campus
nextnrg-nassau-county-data-center-energy.source: NextNRG secures lease for energy and data center campus in Nassau County
nextnrg-nassau-county-data-center-energy.notes: 1,600-acre site (1,200 acres energy / 400 acres data center), 50MW starter phase, with a 6,000-acre expansion option. Nassau County is pursuing a 12-month moratorium in response.

microsoft-firecracker-rome-ga.name: Microsoft Data Center Campus – Rome, GA
microsoft-firecracker-rome-ga.water_notes: No water usage figures or cooling system type disclosed publicly as of 2026-07-07.
microsoft-firecracker-rome-ga.source: Microsoft to develop 350-acre data center campus in Rome, Georgia
microsoft-firecracker-rome-ga.notes: Investment described as '$1 billion' in RFCDA announcement; Data Center Dynamics and Business Facilities use 'more than $1 billion' framing — treated as a floor, not a firm single figure (investmentUsd omitted per data policy). Completion targeted 2027–2028. Site is 347 acres on Huffaker Road, east of Fouche Gap Road, in unincorporated Floyd County, adjacent to Georgia Power-owned land; land purchased at $40,000/acre (~$13.9M). Microsoft stated site selection was driven by 'Rome and Floyd County's industrial zoning and strong infrastructure.' Microsoft committed to covering all costs for additional infrastructure (power, water, roads) so ratepayers and taxpayers are not burdened. Part of Microsoft's broader East US 3 Georgia cloud build-out; announced to bolster Azure cloud services. Floyd County enacted an 80-day moratorium on new data center permits (2025) but explicitly noted previously filed projects including Microsoft's can proceed. Capacity MW not disclosed. Coordinates are approximate; actual parcel is on Huffaker Road in unincorporated Floyd County.

white-oak-technology-park-columbia-count.name: White Oak Technology Park
white-oak-technology-park-columbia-count.source: Plans filed for 8 million sq ft data center and technology park outside Augusta, Georgia
white-oak-technology-park-columbia-count.notes: 8.076M sq ft across up to 29 buildings; 10-year build-out. Zoning rezoned to S-1 (Feb 2026), the first of several required approval steps. Described as a mixed-use tech park (data centers, R&D, cybersecurity), not AI-branded. A second, separate 'Pumpkin Technology Campus' was approved at the same Feb 2026 hearing in nearby Harlem, Columbia County GA - developer not identified in reporting reviewed, flagged as a lead only, not tracked as its own entry. Coordinates are approximate (near Augusta).

google-cedar-rapids-ia.name: Google Cedar Rapids Data Center Campus
google-cedar-rapids-ia.water_notes: Traditional evaporative (water-based) cooling (Daily Iowan, Dec 2025: "the Google center is using the traditional water cooling method"). Estimated use "just over 4 million gallons of water a day" — a pre-operational estimate, not a metered figure. For comparison, Google's Council Bluffs campus averaged ~3.9 MGD.
google-cedar-rapids-ia.source: Google pledges $7bn to expand Iowa data center footprint
google-cedar-rapids-ia.notes: Coordinates approximate for Big Cedar Industrial Center at 76th Ave SW and Edgewood Rd SW in SW Cedar Rapids. Cedar Rapids campus investment ~$576M; part of Google's $7B+ total Iowa commitment announced May/June 2025. Adjacent to QTS campus in same 1,391-acre industrial park. Also exploring a second Linn County campus near Duane Arnold nuclear plant in Palo.

qts-clinton-clinton-county-ia.name: QTS Clinton Data Center Campus
qts-clinton-clinton-county-ia.notes: North of US Highway 30, near Clinton's airport. QTS has not filed a formal site plan; the city is still drafting a data-center ordinance. No confirmed MW or $ figure exists yet - local coverage describes it only as a potential 'multibillion-dollar investment.' Local TV coverage frames this as an 'AI data center' but QTS's own statements avoid the AI label. Coordinates are approximate.

meta-kuna-id.name: Meta Kuna Data Center
meta-kuna-id.source: Meta Resumes Construction of Idaho Data Center with New AI Design
meta-kuna-id.notes: 960,000 sq ft campus (Meta's 15th US data center). Originally Project Peregrine. Construction paused December 2022, restarted October 2023 with AI-optimized architecture; new design 31% cheaper and half the build time. Peak construction employed 1,400 workers. Expected operational end of 2026. Water infrastructure cost sourced to CEG ($70M) but Idaho Business Review cites $100M — discrepancy unresolved; use CEG figure as primary. Coordinates are Kuna city centroid; exact site is west of city center.

element-critical-chicago-one-il.name: Element Critical Chicago One
element-critical-chicago-one-il.notes: Confirmed via operator's own facility page. Address 711 N. Edgewood Avenue, Wood Dale, IL. Operator markets '30 years never down' track record. Distinct site from Chicago Two.

equinix-ch1-il.name: Equinix CH1
equinix-ch1-il.notes: Located at 350 East Cermak Road, downtown Chicago, per Equinix's own Chicago data centers directory; corroborated by baxtel.com and cloudandcolocation.com.

equinix-ch7-il.name: Equinix CH7
equinix-ch7-il.notes: Legacy Verizon facility in Westmont, IL (DuPage County), acquired by Equinix; corroborated by baxtel.com/dgtlinfra.com.

google-fort-wayne-in.name: Google Fort Wayne Data Center (Project Zodiac)
google-fort-wayne-in.powered_by: Grid (Indiana Michigan Power); 188 MW solar PPA (Honeysuckle Solar)
google-fort-wayne-in.source: Gov. Holcomb announces Google is building a $2B Data Center in Northeast Indiana
google-fort-wayne-in.notes: Site near East Tillman Road and Adams Center Road, SE Fort Wayne (Allen County). 700+ acres, multi-building campus explicitly optimized for Gemini AI platform and machine learning. Google STAR workforce program launched with Ivy Tech Community College. Coordinates are approximate site area; exact parcel centroid not verified from public permit records. Previous inkfreenews.com source replaced with WANE 15 which confirmed the same Dec 11 2025 operational story.

sabey-decatur-technology-park-marion-cou.name: Sabey Decatur Technology Park
sabey-decatur-technology-park-marion-cou.source: Sabey targets Indianapolis for 250MW data center campus
sabey-decatur-technology-park-marion-cou.notes: More than one million sq ft, 250MW over a 5-year period. Coordinates are approximate.

markley-lowell-ma.name: Markley Group One Lowell Data Center
markley-lowell-ma.water_notes: 16 evaporative cooling towers, Merrimack River-sourced. Markley self-reports daily use of 60,000-120,000 gallons (0.06-0.12 MGD), peaking ~118,000 gpd in summer, corroborated by WBZ-TV water-bill records - far below hyperscale AI campuses.
markley-lowell-ma.source: Lowell Residents File Massachusetts' First Lawsuit Against a Data Center
markley-lowell-ma.notes: Coordinates are approximate city centroid (Sacred Heart/Back Central neighborhoods, Lowell). Facility serves 100+ customers including hospitals, universities, and police departments. Expansion includes land purchases by Markley near old power plant. Expansion plans stalled by moratorium. AI demand cited as driver of expansion since 2022. Delivered permanent-job counts are disputed - the abatement promised 100 jobs; the city and critics count ~26-30 full-time local workers while Markley cites ~100 total, with construction peaking ~120 (IBEW Local 103); recorded as unresolved (honest-zero). No confirmed total capital-investment figure is public ('hundreds of millions'). Massachusetts' 2024 sales-tax exemption is statutory eligibility, not a confirmed Markley award.

aws-calvert-cliffs-md.name: AWS Calvert County Data Center Campus
aws-calvert-cliffs-md.source: AWS proposes data center campus next to nuclear plant in Calvert County, Maryland
aws-calvert-cliffs-md.notes: Very early-stage: AWS states no formal proposal submitted as of DCD article date. Site plan application filed May 2026. Concept design shared at community open house shows up to 8 buildings south and west of Calvert Cliffs nuclear plant. Capacity not disclosed by AWS. Coordinates approximate for Calvert Cliffs area.

verrus-project-flex-lyon-township-oaklan.name: Project Flex
verrus-project-flex-lyon-township-oaklan.source: Anthropic reported as intended end user of Project Flex data center
verrus-project-flex-lyon-township-oaklan.notes: 6 buildings, 1.8M sq ft. Anthropic (maker of Claude) reported as the intended end-user tenant, not confirmed directly by Anthropic. Conditional site plan approval since Sept 2025. Coordinates are approximate.

avaio-taurus-brandon-ms.name: AVAIO Digital Taurus
avaio-taurus-brandon-ms.water_notes: Operator describes water-efficient cooling, rainwater recapture, cooling system economization (air-side economization implied), and recycled water as an available option. New sewer line extension under construction for wastewater. No specific MGD figure disclosed.
avaio-taurus-brandon-ms.source: AVAIO Digital Taurus announcement press release
avaio-taurus-brandon-ms.notes: Distinct from AVAIO's 'Leo' campus in Little Rock/Pulaski County AR — do not conflate. Site: East Metropolitan Center Business and Industrial Park, Brandon. Land acreage: AVAIO's own project page and groundbreaking materials cite 329 acres; the August 19 press release cited 175 acres — 329 used as more authoritative per operator's site. Capacity: 116 MW initial via executed ESA with Entergy Mississippi (energized June 2027 per operator site); Entergy guiding an additional 420 MW of grid power available by end of 2030; access to Gulf South Pipeline for up to 500 MW of on-site behind-the-meter thermal generation starting Q2 2027 — total baseload path to over 1 GW. The 116 MW planned figure reflects the executed first-phase ESA only; full buildout remains a projection. Investment: $6B stated without 'up to' qualifier across operator, MDA, and Governor's office sources; Governor's office describes it as the third-largest economic development project in Mississippi history. Jobs: 'at least 60 direct, high-tech jobs' and 'hundreds of indirect jobs ranging from construction to other related industries' — projections, not firm figures; no construction vs permanent breakdown confirmed. Rooftop solar of 20+ MW planned (behind-the-meter). Recycled water and new sewer line extension cited by operator as water infrastructure options. Estimated $23M in ad valorem tax revenue annually per Rankin First (county economic development group). Coordinates approximate (Brandon city center, Rankin County).

applied-digital-polaris-forge-2-harwood-.name: Applied Digital Polaris Forge 2
applied-digital-polaris-forge-2-harwood-.powered_by: Cass County Electric Cooperative / Minnkota Power Cooperative
applied-digital-polaris-forge-2-harwood-.utility: Cass County Electric Cooperative / Minnkota Power Cooperative
applied-digital-polaris-forge-2-harwood-.source: Applied Digital to Break Ground on $3 Billion Polaris Forge 2 Campus
applied-digital-polaris-forge-2-harwood-.notes: Two purpose-built facilities totaling more than 1.8 million sq ft. As of the August 2025 announcement, Applied Digital was in advanced negotiations with a U.S.-based investment-grade hyperscaler; no customer or lease value publicly confirmed. Partial operations expected end of 2026; full capacity early 2027. Coordinates are Harwood city centroid; site is approximately 900 acres near this community north of Fargo.

apple-reno-nv.name: Apple Reno Data Center (Reno Technology Park)
apple-reno-nv.powered_by: Turquoise Solar (61 MWdc / ~50MW AC, inside Reno Technology Park adjacent to the Sparks campus) + Fort Churchill Solar (~20MW, near Yerington), delivered via NV Energy's GreenEnergy Rider PPA structure
apple-reno-nv.source: Apple Inc. Board Packet (Data Center Sales & Use Tax Abatement), July 2024 — Apple's own letter: opened Dec 2012, four buildings + substation across 1,700 acres, 200+ staff
apple-reno-nv.notes: Apple data center at 21505 Reno Technology Parkway W, Sparks, Washoe County — the first data center built at the Reno Technology Park, opened December 2012. Per Apple's July 2024 letter in a Nevada GOED tax-abatement board packet, the campus had grown to four data-center buildings plus a power substation across 1,700 acres, with 200+ staff; Apple committed to further investment (a 2024 expansion capex of ~$742M over 5 years / ~$992M over 10 years is documented in the GOED filing). No site-specific IT-load MW is disclosed. Coordinates are an address-level geocode (ArcGIS, exact-address match); a county-parcel pass could upgrade precision to exact.

digital-realty-jfk10-manhattan-ny.name: Digital Realty JFK10 (111 Eighth Avenue)
digital-realty-jfk10-manhattan-ny.notes: 111 Eighth Avenue (the historic 1932 Union Inland Terminal #1 / "Google Building"), Chelsea, Manhattan — Google owns the building; Digital Realty operates JFK10 as a colocation tenant. 111,000 sq ft (Digital Realty's own figure). A third-party estimate of ~18MW capacity is not confirmed by the operator and is omitted. Major carrier hotel with DE-CIX New York and MegaIX New York peering. Coordinates are an approximate geocode of the building, not a confirmed parcel pin.

h5-buffalo-i-lockport-ny.name: H5 Data Centers Buffalo I (formerly Yahoo Lockport)
h5-buffalo-i-lockport-ny.powered_by: Grid-connected; chillerless outside-air cooling design minimizes power draw
h5-buffalo-i-lockport-ny.water_notes: Yahoo's famous "Chicken Coop" design: chillerless, cooled by outside air ~99% of the year with direct evaporative cooling as backup in summer heat, achieving a PUE of 1.08. Not independently reconfirmed as unchanged since the 2025 H5 acquisition.
h5-buffalo-i-lockport-ny.nearest_nuclear_name: R E Ginna Nuclear Power Plant
h5-buffalo-i-lockport-ny.source: H5 Acquires New York Data Centers From Yahoo in Sale-Leaseback Deal
h5-buffalo-i-lockport-ny.notes: 5319 Enterprise Dr, Lockport, NY. Built by Yahoo in 2010 (opened at 155,000 sq ft, expanded since); campus totals 409,200 sq ft / 43 acres SHARED with the separate H5 Buffalo II building (~0.25 mi away — see that record). H5 Data Centers acquired both Lockport buildings from Yahoo in a sale-leaseback deal that closed Dec 30, 2024 ($49M reported); Yahoo signed a 5-year leaseback and remains a tenant on-site (140 staff retained, 15 transferred to H5). Now multi-tenant Tier III colocation, though no tenants beyond Yahoo are independently confirmed. Critical power was 16 MW as of 2014; current total post-expansion not independently disclosed, so capacityMw is deliberately omitted rather than guessed. Coordinates are a campus-level geocode (ConnectBase), not a per-building parcel pin.

niagara-digital-campus-niagara-falls-ny.name: Niagara Digital Campus
niagara-digital-campus-niagara-falls-ny.powered_by: Hydroelectric (NYPA Robert Moses Niagara Power Plant)
niagara-digital-campus-niagara-falls-ny.nearest_nuclear_name: R E Ginna Nuclear Power Plant
niagara-digital-campus-niagara-falls-ny.source: Urbacon: Niagara Digital Campus Data Center
niagara-digital-campus-niagara-falls-ny.notes: Site is near the historic Adams Power Plant and the NYPA Robert Moses Niagara Power Plant (2,675 MW combined capacity). Phase I planned as ~282,000 sq ft over 24 months from groundbreaking. Economic impact estimated at $2B over 20 years per MRB Group analysis commissioned by NFR. Developed by Niagara Falls Redevelopment (NFR, controlled by Milstein family) in partnership with Urbacon.

tierpoint-hawthorne-westchester-ny.name: TierPoint Hawthorne (11 & 17 Skyline Drive)
tierpoint-hawthorne-westchester-ny.source: TierPoint Hawthorne, New York Data Center
tierpoint-hawthorne-westchester-ny.notes: Two adjacent buildings on a shared campus with Westchester County Medical Center and New York Medical College: 11 Skyline Drive (46,000+ sqft total, 28,000+ sqft raised floor, backup generation two 2MW + three 1MW) and 17 Skyline Drive (172,000+ sqft total, 28,000+ sqft raised floor, backup generation two 2,000kW). No whole-campus IT-load MW figure is publicly disclosed — generator specs are backup capacity, not confirmed critical load, so capacityMw is omitted. SOC 1/2 Type II, HITRUST, GLBA, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, NIST SP 800-53, ISO 27001, ITAR-registered. No AI/HPC marketing found. Coordinates are an approximate geocode of the Skyline Drive campus, not a confirmed parcel pin.

aws-scioto-darby-hilliard-oh.name: AWS Scioto Darby Campus
aws-scioto-darby-hilliard-oh.source: AWS planning third data center campus in Hilliard, Ohio
aws-scioto-darby-hilliard-oh.notes: AWS's 3rd Hilliard campus, at 4120 Scioto Darby Rd. 152 acres across 6 parcels, up to 7 buildings plus 1 utility/security building; land bought January 2021 for $15.29M. Distinct from the tracked AWS Cosmos/Galaxy campuses and from the AWS Cosgray Road campus (also in Hilliard).

aligned-neo-01-oh.name: Aligned NEO-01
aligned-neo-01-oh.notes: Confirmed via Aligned's Northeast Ohio page and DatacenterDynamics/JobsOhio press coverage; 2509 Hayes Ave, Sandusky, OH; 96MW/200,000 sq ft, under construction, official name NEO-01. AI/HPC (likely): Sandusky NEO-01 on Aligned DeltaFlow/Delta3 AI/HPC design.

cologix-johnstown-oh.name: Cologix Johnstown AI-Ready Campus
cologix-johnstown-oh.water_notes: Cologix states 'closed-loop cooling systems that minimize water usage' (Columbus Region, June 2026). Under construction - no metered operational figure.
cologix-johnstown-oh.source: Cologix Expands Central Ohio Footprint with Land Acquisition for New AI-Ready 800MW Data Center Campus
cologix-johnstown-oh.notes: 154 acres; up to 800 MW scalable across eight data centers / 2.0M sq ft (800 MW is a full-buildout potential — in notes). The '>$7 billion' figure is a company-wide expansion plan, not a Johnstown-specific committed amount (in notes). Coordinates are the Johnstown, Licking County area centroid. The '>$7B' figure is Cologix's company-wide expansion plan; the $1.17B commitment is combined across Johnstown + Orange Township (not split) -> investmentUsd omitted. Land: ~$45M for 154 acres (Sept 2024).

google-new-albany-oh.name: Google New Albany Data Center
google-new-albany-oh.notes: 1101 Beech Rd SW, New Albany — operated via Google's Ohio subsidiary Montauk Innovations LLC. 275,000 sq ft initial building on a ~440-447 acre campus. $600M confirmed initial capital investment; 100% real-property tax abatement (15yr) and 100% sales-tax exemption (~$43.5M value, 15yr) granted. Distinct from Google's Lima "Project BOSC" facility (different county) and Google's Lancaster campus (tracked separately). No IT-load MW figure publicly disclosed. In June 2025, the same Montauk Innovations entity acquired an adjacent 85-acre parcel at 2565 Harrison Road NW (~4 miles north) for $63M; Google has NOT confirmed this parcel will become a data center ("we want to ensure we have the option to further grow, should our business demand it" per a spokesperson) — tracked as a note here rather than a standalone facility pending confirmation. No AI/HPC-specific marketing found — Google's own materials describe this and its other Ohio campuses generically as cloud/digital infrastructure. County-auditor parcels confirm the campus straddles the Franklin-Licking line: the operational, data-center-classed parcel is in Franklin County (5266 Babbitt Rd, 222 ac, Montauk Innovations LLC, acquired Dec 2018 for $27.4M), extending east across the line into Licking County at 1101 Beech Rd SW (219 ac; ~441 ac combined). The coordinate is now parcel-exact to the Franklin operational parcel.

prologis-mila-trenton-oh.name: Prologis Project Mila
prologis-mila-trenton-oh.source: Prologis details plans for data center campus outside Cincinnati, Ohio
prologis-mila-trenton-oh.notes: Project Mila in Trenton, Butler County (outside Cincinnati): four 220,000 sq ft single-story buildings (880k sq ft total) plus an on-site substation. Planning approved March 2026; construction from fall 2026. Estimated ~100-200 MW (not officially disclosed — omitted from capacity). Distinct from Prologis's Newnan, GA campus. Coordinates are the Trenton area centroid.

qts-new-albany-3-franklin-county-oh.name: QTS New Albany III
qts-new-albany-3-franklin-county-oh.source: Franklin County parcel/GIS record (parcel 222-005361 — QTS NEW ALBANY III LLC, use-class "data center", 78.01 ac)
qts-new-albany-3-franklin-county-oh.notes: Third QTS campus in the New Albany International Business Park, on Babbitt Rd (Franklin County) — 3 buildings, ~1.1M sq ft on 78 acres, announced December 2023 alongside the Miller Rd (IV) site as part of QTS's ~$4.4B New Albany expansion (aggregate across III + IV; no reliable per-site investment split disclosed, so investmentUsd omitted). Franklin County auditor use-class is "data center" (an assessed data-center structure exists); construction status is not independently confirmed operational by press, so recorded conservatively as under_construction. Distinct from QTS New Albany I & II (Beech Rd SW). No site-specific IT-load MW disclosed.

beltline-piedmont-kingfisher-county-ok.name: Beltline Energy Piedmont Site
beltline-piedmont-kingfisher-county-ok.notes: 321-acre rezoning filed via BLE Holdings LLC / BLE Landholdings LLC, SW/4 of Section 26, Township 15N, Range 6W, Kingfisher County — legal descriptions and Kingfisher County parcel numbers 0000-26-15N-06W-3-000-00, -3-001-00, -3-002-00, -3-003-00 (plus an adjacent 5th parcel, -4-000-00) per the city's own PUD filing. Bounded by E 870 Rd (N), N 2920 Rd (E), Azalea St NW (S), N 2910 Rd (W). City vote delayed for further review as of source date. This is a distinct, separate, competing site from Cloverleaf's 630-acre 'Project Open Sky' proposal also in Piedmont (different parcels, different developer, different acreage) — despite sharing a host city, do not conflate the two (both independently confirmed as separate projects via direct source verification). No primary-sourced capacity or investment figure was found for this specific site — omitted rather than guessed.

cerebras-oklahoma-city-ok.name: Cerebras Oklahoma City Data Center
cerebras-oklahoma-city-ok.water_notes: Direct-to-chip liquid cooling via closed-loop system; Cerebras describes it as minimizing water consumption. Custom water-cooling solution designed for CS-3 wafer-scale servers. No mgd figure disclosed.
cerebras-oklahoma-city-ok.source: Cerebras Unveils Six Data Centers to Meet Accelerating Demand for AI Inference at Scale
cerebras-oklahoma-city-ok.notes: Colocation tenancy: Cerebras Systems is the AI infrastructure operator; Scale Datacenters is the facility host/colo provider (acquired the 82,000 sq ft building from Expand Energy, formerly Chesapeake Energy, originally built ~2013). Facility address: 512 NW 62nd St (corner of NW 61st/62nd St and N Lee Ave), Oklahoma City. Ribbon cutting September 22, 2025. Houses 300+ CS-3 Wafer Scale Engine systems delivering 44+ exaflops of AI compute. Facility features Tier III-quality infrastructure, tornado and seismic shielding, triple-redundant power stations. Cerebras matches all kWh consumption with renewable energy (REC-based, not on-site generation). OG&E reported as grid utility — consistent with OKC service territory but not explicitly named in Cerebras primary sources. Investment amount not disclosed. Jobs: Cerebras blog references 'hundreds of good-paying jobs' in engineering, IT, and operations plus local college workforce partnerships — no firm headcount confirmed. Coordinates are approximate (dispatch seed); actual facility is at 512 NW 62nd St.

flexential-portland-hillsboro-1-pdx01-or.name: Flexential Portland - Hillsboro 1 (PDX01)
flexential-portland-hillsboro-1-pdx01-or.notes: 3935 NE Aloclek Dr Building C, Hillsboro OR, 5.3MW (PDX01) per DataCenterJournal/baxtel.

google-the-dalles-or.name: Google The Dalles Data Center Campus
google-the-dalles-or.water_notes: City records released after a 2021–22 public-records lawsuit — which the city, funded by Google (>$100K), later dropped — show Google consumed 355.1M gallons in 2021 (~29% of The Dalles' total water use), up from 104.3M gallons in 2012. Google committed $28.5M to upgrade city water infrastructure.
google-the-dalles-or.source: The Dalles, Oregon — Google data centers (Wikipedia)

ntt-hillsboro-hi1-data-center-or.name: NTT Hillsboro HI1 Data Center
ntt-hillsboro-hi1-data-center-or.notes: 4050 NE Evergreen Rd; 36MW, first of a planned 5-building/126MW campus; building acquired from SunPower in 2019.

coreweave-lancaster-pa.name: CoreWeave Lancaster Data Center
coreweave-lancaster-pa.water_notes: Air-cooled, closed-loop design; the developer states no municipal water will be used in cooling. The community benefits agreement caps water at 20,000 gal/day per campus — a claimed >80% reduction from the former printing plants on the sites.
coreweave-lancaster-pa.source: CoreWeave Announces Multi-Billion Dollar Commitment to AI Infrastructure in Pennsylvania — CoreWeave

expedient-pit1-green-tree-pittsburgh-sou.name: Expedient PIT1 (Green Tree / Pittsburgh South)
expedient-pit1-green-tree-pittsburgh-sou.source: Expedient official Pittsburgh data center page
expedient-pit1-green-tree-pittsburgh-sou.notes: 810 Parish St, Pittsburgh, PA 15220 (Green Tree neighborhood). Site code PIT1, 1.8MW critical IT load, 26,000 sq ft. 'Pittsburgh South' is the OSM/aggregator alias (confirmed same address on datacentermap.com) -- this is Expedient's official PIT1/Green Tree facility, distinct from PIT2/North Shore which is not among the candidates.

flexential-allentown-data-center-abe01-p.name: Flexential Allentown Data Center (ABE01)
flexential-allentown-data-center-abe01-p.notes: 744 Roble Rd, Allentown PA (ABE01), formerly ViaWest/Peak10 per baxtel/UPSTACK corroboration.

lumen-norristown-pa.name: Lumen Norristown
lumen-norristown-pa.notes: Baxtel-listed as an operational Lumen facility; exact street address not surfaced but facility existence and operator confirmed.

google-winding-woods-st-george-sc.name: Google Winding Woods Campus
google-winding-woods-st-george-sc.source: Google to invest $9bn in South Carolina data centers
google-winding-woods-st-george-sc.notes: Google's second SC campus, in Winding Woods Commerce Park, St. George, Dorchester County; part of a $9B South Carolina investment (statewide figure — not a single-campus capex). Distinct from Google's Ridgeville, SC campus. IT capacity not disclosed. Coordinates are the St. George area centroid.

bitdeer-knoxville-tn.name: Bitdeer Knoxville AI Datacenter (5101 S. National Drive)
bitdeer-knoxville-tn.source: Bitdeer Technologies Group FY2025 Form 20-F, filed 2026-04-30
bitdeer-knoxville-tn.notes: Existing Bitmain/Bitdeer Bitcoin mining site operational since May 2020 (property acquired 2018 via Commercial Purchase and Sale Agreement with Kemet Foil Manufacturing LLC, 9.88 acres / 77,678 sq ft industrial building). The 20-F discloses an active conversion to AI cloud use: Phase 1 (37MW) targeted Q4 2026, Phase 2 (49MW) targeted Q1 2027, against 86MW total electrical capacity in use as of 2026-03-31. Coordinates are an approximate parcel-area estimate for the South National Drive industrial corridor in Knox County (near APN 110-02627 per public tax-assessment/LoopNet listing) since no geocoder was available in-session to pin the exact parcel centroid — flagging for a follow-up precision pass if the site is approved. Crypto-mining site converting to AI (Bitdeer 20-F): Phase 1 37 MW targeted Q4 2026, Phase 2 49 MW Q1 2027; zero AI capacity live today (the existing 86 MW is legacy mining load being phased out).

cielo-clarksville-tn.name: Cielo Montgomery County AI Campus
cielo-clarksville-tn.notes: ~107-acre proposed site, ~350 MW. Distinct operator/parcel from Google's operational Clarksville (Montgomery County) campus. Sourcing is thin (tracker + developer site) → confidence reported. Cielo specializes in power/fiber-ready campus development. Coordinates are the Clarksville area centroid.

xai-colossus-memphis-tn.name: Colossus
xai-colossus-memphis-tn.water_notes: The open cooling loop's design draw is roughly 3 MGD from the Memphis Sands aquifer via MLGW (xAI engineer, per Governing), though Protect Our Aquifer reported a lower early-operational actual of ~0.8 MGD (~812,000 gal/day) in early 2025 as the site was still ramping. xAI broke ground in Oct 2025 on an $80M greywater-recycling plant at the T.E. Maxson wastewater facility (targeting ~10 MGD of treated wastewater); construction was later paused.

meta-gallatin-tn.name: Meta Gallatin Data Center Campus
meta-gallatin-tn.water_notes: Direct air cooling (outside air + fan technology), no conventional AC units; "use 80% less water than a typical data center" (w.media). Goal of being water-positive by 2030. No site-specific MGD figure published.
meta-gallatin-tn.source: Meta brings data centers in tents to Gallatin, Tennessee
meta-gallatin-tn.notes: Campus coordinates are city-centroid approximation for Gallatin, TN. Up to 12 data halls planned on 900+ acres per DPR Construction (general contractor). Meta is deploying AI GPU clusters in waterproof tent structures (rapid deployment structures) at this campus to accelerate capacity ahead of permanent building construction.

aligned-dfw-01-tx.name: Aligned DFW-01
aligned-dfw-01-tx.notes: Confirmed operational on Aligned's Dallas directory page; address 2800 Summit Ave, Plano, TX 75074. AI/HPC (likely): Dallas DFW-01: Aligned DeltaFlow/Delta3 high-density AI/HPC platform.

cyrusone-sat2-sat4-san-antonio-tx.name: CyrusOne SAT2-SAT4 (San Antonio)
cyrusone-sat2-sat4-san-antonio-tx.notes: OSM label 'San Antonio II' resolved to SAT2-SAT4 campus (9554 Westover Hills Blvd / 9655 Raba Dr). AI/HPC (likely): HPC spec: over 1,000 watts/sqft in designated areas.

data-city-energy-abundance-laredo-tx.name: Data City, Texas
data-city-energy-abundance-laredo-tx.source: Energy Abundance announces Data City, Texas (press release, Mar 21 2025)
data-city-energy-abundance-laredo-tx.notes: Early-stage developer announcement (Mar 21 2025) for a 5 GW behind-the-meter data center hub on ~50,000 acres near Laredo (Webb County), targeting large AI workloads with direct-to-chip liquid cooling. Phase 1 stated as 300 MW / ~1M sq ft in 2026, scaling to 5 GW / 15M+ sq ft. Highly speculative: primary source is a single promotional press release; no permit, interconnection, or construction evidence located. Coordinate anchored on Laredo.

element-critical-austin-one-tx.name: Element Critical Austin One
element-critical-austin-one-tx.notes: Confirmed via operator's own official facility page and current brochure PDF (elementcritical.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/...). Address 8025 N Interstate Hwy 35, Austin, TX 78753. 5MW, 62,300 sq ft.

fort-spunky-pacifico-energy-hood-county-.name: Fort Spunky
fort-spunky-pacifico-energy-hood-county-.source: Texas data centers: Hood County, local control, rural water and power
fort-spunky-pacifico-energy-hood-county-.notes: 862 acres, across the Brazos River from the Pecan Plantation community. Water draw up to 20,000 gal/day. Coordinates are approximate.

iren-horizon-childress-tx.name: IREN Horizon — Childress, TX
iren-horizon-childress-tx.water_notes: Direct-to-chip closed-loop liquid cooling. IREN states the system does not consume water on an ongoing basis; annual top-ups require roughly as much water as a few houses. Water is trucked in externally — deliberately not drawn from Childress municipal supply. System described as analogous to a vehicle radiator.
iren-horizon-childress-tx.source: IREN plans 75MW liquid-cooled AI data center in Texas
iren-horizon-childress-tx.notes: SEPARATE SITE from IREN Sweetwater (Nolan/Fisher County — do not conflate). Full 750 MW figure is total campus transmission capacity; the AI/Microsoft Horizon 1–4 build-out comprises four 50 MW IT (75 MW gross) liquid-cooled data halls = 200 MW IT total, targeting end-2026 delivery. Horizon 1 (50 MW IT / 75 MW gross) energized Q4 2025 — operational; Horizons 2–4 remain under construction as of mid-2026. Coordinates approximate (county seat area). Site is a 576-acre freehold parcel with on-site 345 kV substations connecting directly to ERCOT. Investment for Horizon 1–4 reported as $300–350M (range; not a firm figure — omitted from investmentUsd). Microsoft contract ($9.7B total, 5-year through ~2031) covers NVIDIA GB300 Blackwell Ultra GPU cloud services; 20% upfront prepayment funded capex. Dell Technologies hardware supply agreement: $5.8B. IREN also holds a separate NVIDIA cloud services contract at Childress. Rack density 130–200 kW per rack; projected PUE 1.05–1.10. Approximately 25 current full-time local employees, 50+ expected at 750 MW full build-out; over 500 contractors during construction phase (approximate reported figures — omitted from jobs numeric fields). IREN Community Grants Program distributes $250,000 annually to the Childress area.

iren-sweetwater-tx.name: IREN Sweetwater Campus
iren-sweetwater-tx.water_notes: Direct-to-chip liquid cooling plus supplemental air cooling. Closed-loop design described by IREN and analysts as dramatically reducing water consumption vs. traditional evaporative approaches. West Texas arid climate noted as a water-conservation design driver. No reported MGD figure confirmed.
iren-sweetwater-tx.source: IREN Announces Successful Energization of Sweetwater 1
iren-sweetwater-tx.notes: Two-site campus: Sweetwater 1 (1,400 MW, ~1,700 acres, Nolan/Jones County boundary area) substation energized May 1, 2026 via 345kV ERCOT connection; data centers commissioning in phases. Sweetwater 2 (600 MW, ~500 acres, Fisher County, near Hamlin TX, ~28 miles from SW1) targeted energization late 2027 per IREN (some sources cite 2028). Direct fiber loop planned between sites for single 2 GW compute hub with <10ms latency to Dallas. Coordinates are approximate (Sweetwater city center, Nolan County seat). County boundary sources conflicting: DCD says Fisher County for both sites; interconnection.fyi and dispatch brief cite Nolan County for SW1; northwiseproject.com says Nolan and Jones Counties span the campus. IREN's $9.7B Microsoft contract (Nov 2025) and $3.4B NVIDIA contract (May 2026) are company-wide deals currently deployed at Childress, TX campus (Horizon 1-4); the NVIDIA partnership press release specifically names Sweetwater as the flagship future deployment site for NVIDIA DSX factory architecture. No confirmed customer contracts specific to Sweetwater site as of 2026-07-07. IREN was in Sweetwater since 2022 as a Bitcoin mining site; HPC/AI pivot announced October 2024. Interconnection.fyi lists renewable energy sourcing via RECs (wind/solar) at this site.

microsoft-san-antonio-expansion-tx.name: Microsoft San Antonio SAT89/SAT90 Data Centers
microsoft-san-antonio-expansion-tx.water_notes: Microsoft switched the Medina County design from evaporative to air-cooling at the request of Yancey Water Supply (which serves the area), cutting projected water use ~85% (~150,000 gpd). No site-specific residual water-use (MGD) figure is published.
microsoft-san-antonio-expansion-tx.source: Microsoft files for data center campus outside San Antonio
microsoft-san-antonio-expansion-tx.notes: Two single-story facilities (SAT89 and SAT90), each 244,700 sq ft, along US Hwy 90 in Medina County. Part of Microsoft's broader San Antonio campus (operating since 2005). $765M investment covers the two new buildings; broader expansion including Texas Research Park adds another $1B. Coordinates are approximate Castroville area centroid; exact parcel not publicly identified. Completion target corrected to July 2027 per permit filings. Tax abatements for SAT89/SAT90 are shielded under Texas competitive-information law (a Chapter 312 abatement is confirmed only for the earlier SAT82 building); site-specific job counts are unpublished (an earlier SAT82 building cited ~50 permanent / ~1,500 construction).

galaxy-digital-mcgregor-tx.name: Project Merlin (Helios II)
galaxy-digital-mcgregor-tx.source: Galaxy Digital AI data center announced in McGregor, Texas
galaxy-digital-mcgregor-tx.notes: ~500MW initial phase, up to 3,500MW long-term. 500 acres NE of the SpaceX facility. Second Galaxy Digital Texas site, distinct from the tracked Afton/Dickens County Helios campus.

databank-red-oak-tx.name: Red Oak Campus
databank-red-oak-tx.source: DataBank lands $2 billion loan for Dallas data center expansion
databank-red-oak-tx.notes: 292-acre, 8-building campus. Distinct operator/site from Compass Datacenters' separate Red Oak, TX campus (same town, different companies).

soluna-project-kati-willacy-tx.name: Soluna Project Kati
soluna-project-kati-willacy-tx.nearest_power_name: Magic Valley Wind Farm I LLC
soluna-project-kati-willacy-tx.source: Soluna Breaks Ground on its Largest Site to Date, Project Kati
soluna-project-kati-willacy-tx.notes: Rio Grande Valley, Willacy County; 166 MW clean computing in two phases (scaling toward 300+ MW — in notes), ERCOT-approved, Phase 1 live early 2026. Coordinates are anchored to Raymondville (county seat); the exact parcel is unspecified.

stargate-abilene-tx.name: Stargate Abilene
stargate-abilene-tx.water_notes: Direct-to-chip liquid cooling with a zero-water-evaporation closed-loop system (per Measured AI, ~12,625 gallons per building per year). Mayor stated the facility would use less than 1% of Abilene's daily water. reportedMgd omitted — only per-building annual volume disclosed.

vantage-frontier-shackelford-county-tx.name: Vantage Frontier Campus
vantage-frontier-shackelford-county-tx.water_notes: Vantage describes a closed-loop chilled-water system with 'near zero' water utilization efficiency; no reported MGD figure disclosed.
vantage-frontier-shackelford-county-tx.source: Vantage Data Centers Unveils Plans for Frontier, a $25B Mega-campus in Texas — Vantage

flexential-salt-lake-city-lindon-ut.name: Flexential Salt Lake City - Lindon
flexential-salt-lake-city-lindon-ut.notes: HIPAA/HITRUST/PCI-DSS certified facility per WebSearch corroboration; distinct from South Valley/West Jordan site.

joule-millard-county-ut.name: Joule Energy and Data Center Campus
joule-millard-county-ut.powered_by: On-site Caterpillar G3520K gas generators; nuclear planned post-2030
joule-millard-county-ut.water_notes: Closed-loop direct-to-chip cooling saves millions of gallons vs evaporative; family water rights held by founders; no new water allocation required
joule-millard-county-ut.source: Groundbreaking held for Joule data center campus in Millard County
joule-millard-county-ut.notes: Founders Mark McDougal and David Gray converting family 4,000-acre alfalfa farm near Holden. Described by founders as largest private project in Utah history. Partnership with Caterpillar for generator sets; MOU with EnergySolutions for nuclear feasibility study. Part of Governor Cox's Operation Gigawatt initiative. Site at 4,800+ ft elevation for cooling efficiency. Coordinates approximate for Holden, Millard County.

aws-mattermeade-caroline-va.name: AWS Mattermeade Tech Campus
aws-mattermeade-caroline-va.source: Amazon requests permit for 11-building data center campus in Caroline County, Virginia
aws-mattermeade-caroline-va.notes: 1,143 acres across Caroline & Spotsylvania counties, SE of the I-95 / Mudd Tavern Rd interchange; 11 two-story data center buildings plus an office. Amazon is 'seeking to develop a minimum of 770 MW by 2027'. Recorded as proposed (federal permit application filed / public-comment stage as of early 2025). Coordinates are the Bowling Green / Woodford area centroid.

bermuda-hundred-data-center-chesterfield.name: Bermuda Hundred Data Center (Old Bermuda Hundred Road)
bermuda-hundred-data-center-chesterfield.source: Chesterfield Zoning Appeals Board denies appeal over proposed data center campus near I-95
bermuda-hundred-data-center-chesterfield.notes: Proposed data center on ~89 acres at 1931 Old Bermuda Hundred Rd, Chester (Bermuda District), Chesterfield County. Land owned by Washington Single Family Fund3 (acquired 2023 for $462,000); the data-center developer is undisclosed. Under the pre-2026 I-2 zoning it was by-right; the 2026 ordinance made data centers conditional-use. The planning director found no vested right and the BZA unanimously upheld that denial 2026-06-03, so a CUP is now required. Recorded as proposed (not cancelled) with community=litigation.

digital-realty-iad55-va.name: Digital Realty IAD55
digital-realty-iad55-va.source: Baxtel/marketplace listings confirming IAD55 as an active Digital Realty Ashburn/Sterling-area building code

digital-realty-northern-virginia-acc5-va.name: Digital Realty Northern Virginia ACC5
digital-realty-northern-virginia-acc5-va.source: Digital Realty official Northern Virginia facilities page (verified via WebFetch)
digital-realty-northern-virginia-acc5-va.notes: Address 44521 Hastings Drive, Ashburn, VA 20147 — distinct from ACC4 (480 Hastings Dr).

corscale-gainesville-crossing-va.name: Gainesville Crossing Digital Campus (GCDC)
corscale-gainesville-crossing-va.developer: Corscale Data Centers (Patrinely / USAA Real Estate)
corscale-gainesville-crossing-va.water_notes: Air-cooled chillers (Airedale by Modine) with liquid-cooled options available; LEED / water-use-efficiency targets. No confirmed operational daily-use figure published.
corscale-gainesville-crossing-va.source: New hyperscale developer Corscale is behind 300MW Gainesville Crossing campus in Prince William County
corscale-gainesville-crossing-va.notes: ~130-acre campus on Interstate 66; ~306 MW via an on-site Dominion substation. Distinct from the separately-tracked QTS/Compass 'PW Digital Gateway' site (~2,100 acres at Pageland Lane) — which QTS terminated in July 2026. Capacity recorded at 300 MW per the DCD primary source (a 326 MW figure also circulates). Coordinates are the Gainesville area centroid. The only confirmed money figure is the ~$74.5M 2020 land purchase (a real-estate transaction, not construction capex) -> investmentUsd omitted; no headcount is disclosed; the VA sales-and-use tax exemption is eligibility-gated with no public award.

google-loch-midlothian-va.name: Google Project Loch
google-loch-midlothian-va.water_notes: Site adjacent to Tomahawk Creek (Chesapeake Bay watershed). Army Corps permit (May 2026) covers ~5 acres of wetlands and 2,828 ft of stream channels; proposed mitigation ~11 acres of replacement wetlands + 34.2 acres preserved.
google-loch-midlothian-va.source: Google files for data center campus outside Richmond, Virginia
google-loch-midlothian-va.notes: Codename Project Loch; land acquired via shell entity Aeris Investments LLC (~$29M for ~340 acres). Site: 750 Watkins Centre Pkwy (Watkins Centre South), west of Rt 288 and south of Rt 60, near Westchester Commons. Three data-center buildings planned, each with a dedicated on-site substation. Google stated in Aug 2025 it has no near-term plans to develop Loch. Capacity MW not disclosed. Virginia law bars per-company subsidy value disclosure, so the 30-year fixed tax agreement is recorded as a program label with no dollar value. Coordinates are an approximate site centroid (address-derived, not GPS-verified).

aws-lake-anna-technology-campus-louisa-v.name: Lake Anna Technology Campus (LATC)
aws-lake-anna-technology-campus-louisa-v.developer: Amazon Web Services (with REB Investment Company, LLC as landowner)
aws-lake-anna-technology-campus-louisa-v.source: Louisa County land-disturbance permit + VA DEQ stormwater permit (reported via county-sourced local coverage)
aws-lake-anna-technology-campus-louisa-v.notes: One of two AWS campuses in Louisa's Technology Overlay District (approved by BOS April 2023, ~$11B combined investment across both). Up to seven data center buildings (~1.7M sq ft), two 300MW substations. First DC targeted online late 2025/early 2026. A third AWS Louisa campus proposal (1,370 acres near Northeast Creek Reservoir) was withdrawn/cancelled by AWS in July 2025 — not included per do-not-fabricate rule (cancelled, not net-new). Capacity corrected to 600 MW (two 300 MW substations per Louisa County reporting; a prior 420 MW figure was unsourced). Land-disturbance + VA DEQ stormwater permits issued; grading underway.

lumen-ashburn-va.name: Lumen Ashburn
lumen-ashburn-va.notes: Baxtel-listed 'Lumen Ashburn' facility, built 2016, Data Center Alley; legacy Level3 branding matches OSM 'Level 3 Ashburn'.

lumen-mclean-1-va.name: Lumen McLean 1
lumen-mclean-1-va.notes: 1755 Old Meadow Road, McLean, VA. Corroborated via datacenters.com/baxtel/datacentermap (Lumen legacy Level3 McLean1).

ntt-ashburn-va8-data-center-va.name: NTT Ashburn VA8 Data Center
ntt-ashburn-va8-data-center-va.source: NTT Global Data Centers Americas facility directory
ntt-ashburn-va8-data-center-va.notes: Part of NTT's 78-acre, 224MW Ashburn campus (Data Center Alley, Loudoun County). Confirmed via NTT's own Ashburn locations page; a dedicated VA8-specific NTT page was not directly loaded but multiple third-party listings (datacentermap.com, datacenterhawk.com) corroborate VA8 as a real, distinct building on the NTT Ashburn campus.

amazon-potomac-church-fredericksburg-va.name: Potomac Church Technology Center
amazon-potomac-church-fredericksburg-va.source: Stafford County zoning/substation case — Potomac Church

bitdeer-wenatchee-pangborn-wa.name: Bitdeer Wenatchee (Pangborn) Data Center
bitdeer-wenatchee-pangborn-wa.source: Bitdeer Technologies Group FY2025 Form 20-F (filed 2026-04-30) — Item 4.D Property: Pangborn, Washington datacenter, 13 MW, operational May 2018, being converted to AI cloud (GB300 cluster; permits submitted; crypto dismantling began March 2026; target Q4 2026)
bitdeer-wenatchee-pangborn-wa.notes: Bitdeer's Washington datacenter, referred to as "Pangborn, Washington" in its SEC filings (Pangborn Memorial Airport is in Douglas County, East Wenatchee) and as "Wenatchee, Washington" by aggregators. Originally deployed for Bitcoin mining in May 2018; 13 MW electrical capacity in use as of March 31, 2026. Bitdeer is converting the site to AI cloud use: AI datacenter design documents and building-permit applications submitted, core equipment being delivered, planned to begin with an NVIDIA GB300 cluster; dismantling of the crypto mining datacenter began March 2026 with conversion completion targeted for Q4 2026. Classified data_center (mid-conversion to AI), consistent with the tracked Bitdeer Knoxville TN conversion. Coordinates approximate (Pangborn area, Douglas County). Distinct from Bitdeer's tracked Ohio (Massillon/Clarington/Niles/Shalersville), Texas (Rockdale) and Tennessee (Knoxville) sites.
